avalancheActivity.highlights: Wind slabs represent the main danger.
avalancheActivity.comment:
The wind slabs can be released even by a single winter sport participant in particular on steep shady slopes. The avalanches can reach medium size. Adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls and at the base of rock walls the likelihood of avalanches is higher. The prevalence of avalanche prone locations and likelihood of triggering will increase with altitude.

Weak layers in the lower part of the snowpack can be released in some places. This applies on steep shady slopes above approximately 2400 m.

In particular on very steep sunny slopes and in steep rocky terrain small dry and moist avalanches are possible as a consequence of solar radiation.
The Avalanche Warning Service currently has only a small amount of information that has been collected in the field, so that the avalanche danger should be investigated especially thoroughly in the relevant locality.

snowpackStructure.comment:
5 to 30 cm of snow has fallen since Wednesday above approximately 1600 m. As a consequence of new snow and a moderate wind from variable directions, wind slabs formed adjacent to ridgelines and in gullies and bowls.

Avalanche prone weak layers exist in the old snowpack. Whumpfing sounds and the formation of shooting cracks when stepping on the snowpack and fresh avalanches serve as an alarm sign.

Below approximately 2000 m only a little snow is lying.
